cherry.help: A synonym for --right-only --cherry-mark --no-merges; useful to limit the output to the commits on our side and mark those that have been applied to the other side of a forked history with git log --cherry upstream...mybranch, similar to git cherry upstream mybranch

color_moved.help: Moved lines of code are colored differently

color_moved_ws.help: This configures how whitespace is ignored when performing the move detection for --color-moved

color_words.help: Equivalent to --word-diff=color plus (if a regex was specified) --word-diff-regex=<regex>

date.help: Only takes effect for dates shown in human-readable format, such as when using --pretty

date_order.help: Show no parents before all of its children are shown, but otherwise show commits in the commit timestamp order

dd.help: Produce diff with respect to first parent for both merge and regular commits

default_prefix.help: Use the default source and destination prefixes ("a/" and "b/")

dense.help: Only the selected commits are shown, plus some to have a meaningful history

diff_merges.help: Specify diff format to be used for merge commits

dirstat.help: Output the distribution of relative amount of changes for each sub-directory

dst_prefix.help: Show the given destination <prefix> instead of "b/"

exclude.help: Do not include refs matching <glob-pattern> that the next --all, --branches, --tags, --remotes, or --glob would otherwise consider

exclude_first_parent_only.help: When finding commits to exclude (with a ^), follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit

exclude_hidden.help: Do not include refs that would be hidden by git-fetch, git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack by consulting the appropriate fetch.hideRefs, receive.hideRefs or uploadpack.hideRefs configuration along with transfer.hideRefs (see git-config(1))

ext_diff.help: Allow an external diff helper to be executed

extended_regexp.help: Consider the limiting patterns to be extended regular expressions instead of the default basic regular expressions

find_copies.help: Detect copies as well as renames

find_copies_harder.help: For performance reasons, by default, -C option finds copies only if the original file of the copy was modified in the same changeset

find_object.help: Look for differences that change the number of occurrences of the specified object

find_renames.help: If generating diffs, detect and report renames for each commit

first_parent.help: When finding commits to include, follow only the first parent commit upon seeing a merge commit

ignore_space_at_eol.help: Ignore changes in whitespace at EOL

ignore_submodules.help: Ignore changes to submodules in the diff generation

indent_heuristic.help: Enable the heuristic that shifts diff hunk boundaries to make patches easier to read

inter_hunk_context.help: Show the context between diff hunks, up to the specified <number> of lines, thereby fusing hunks that are close to each other

invert_grep.help: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that do not match the <pattern> specified with --grep=<pattern>

ita_invisible_in_index.help: By default entries added by git add -N appear as an existing empty file in git diff and a new file in git diff --cached

no_walk.help: Only show the given commits, but do not traverse their ancestors

not.help: Reverses the meaning of the ^ prefix (or lack thereof) for all following revision specifiers, up to the next --not

src_prefix.help: Show the given source <prefix> instead of "a/"

stdin.help: In addition to getting arguments from the command line, read them from standard input as well

summary.help: Output a condensed summary of extended header information such as creations, renames and mode changes

unified.help: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context

merged.help: Only list tags whose commits are reachable from <commit> (HEAD if not specified)

n.help: <num> specifies how many lines from the annotation, if any, are printed when using -l

no_contains.help: Only list tags which don't contain <commit> (HEAD if not specified)

b.help: With add, create a new branch named <new-branch> starting at <commit-ish>, and check out <new-branch> into the new worktree

checkout.help: By default, add checks out <commit-ish>, however, --no-checkout can be used to suppress checkout in order to make customizations, such as configuring sparse-checkout

detach.help: With add, detach HEAD in the new worktree

dry_run.help: With prune, do not remove anything; just report what it would remove

expire.help: With prune, only prune missing worktrees if older than <time>

force.help: By default, add refuses to create a new worktree when <commit-ish> is a branch name and is already checked out by another worktree, or if <path> is already assigned to some worktree but is missing (for instance, if <path> was deleted manually)

guess_remote.help: With worktree add <path>, without <commit-ish>, instead of creating a new branch from HEAD, if there exists a tracking branch in exactly one remote matching the basename of <path>, base the new branch on the remote-tracking branch, and mark the remote-tracking branch as "upstream" from the new branch

lock.help: Keep the worktree locked after creation

orphan.help: With add, make the new worktree and index empty, associating the worktree with a new unborn branch named <new-branch>

porcelain.help: With list, output in an easy-to-parse format for scripts

reason.help: With lock or with add --lock, an explanation why the worktree is locked

relative_paths.help: Link worktrees using relative paths or absolute paths (default)

track.help: When creating a new branch, if <commit-ish> is a branch, mark it as "upstream" from the new branch

z.help: Terminate each line with a NUL rather than a newline when --porcelain is specified with list

fetch\tnegotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

pull\tnegotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

fetch\tall.help: Fetch all remotes, except for the ones that has the remote.<name>.skipFetchAll configuration variable set

fetch\tnegotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip= arguments, which we have in common with the server

pull\tnegotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip= arguments, which we have in common with the server

switch\tmerge.help: If you have local modifications to one or more files that are different between the current branch and the branch to which you are switching, the command refuses to switch branches in order to preserve your modifications in context

clone\tbranch.help: Instead of pointing the newly created HEAD to the branch pointed to by the cloned repository's HEAD, point to <name> branch instead

clone\tno_checkout.help: No checkout of HEAD is performed after the clone is complete

clone\tprogress.help: Progress status is reported on the standard error stream by default when it is attached to a terminal, unless --quiet is specified

clone\tupload_pack.help: When given, and the repository to clone from is accessed via ssh, this specifies a non-default path for the command run on the other end

diff\tunified.help: Generate diffs with <n> lines of context instead of the usual three

worktree\texpire.help: With prune, only expire unused worktrees older than <time>

commit\tnull.help: When showing short or porcelain status output, print the filename verbatim and terminate the entries with NUL, instead of LF

fetch\tjobs.help: Number of parallel children to be used for all forms of fetching

fetch\tnegotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip=* arguments, which we have in common with the server

fetch\trefmap.help: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.*.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository

pull\tjobs.help: Number of parallel children to be used for all forms of fetching

pull\tnegotiate_only.help: Do not fetch anything from the server, and instead print the ancestors of the provided --negotiation-tip=* arguments, which we have in common with the server

pull\tnegotiation_tip.help: By default, Git will report, to the server, commits reachable from all local refs to find common commits in an attempt to reduce the size of the to-be-received packfile

pull\trebase.help: When true, rebase the current branch on top of the upstream branch after fetching

pull\trefmap.help: When fetching refs listed on the command line, use the specified refspec (can be given more than once) to map the refs to remote-tracking branches, instead of the values of remote.*.fetch configuration variables for the remote repository

commit\tverify.help: Bypass the pre-commit and commit-msg hooks

log\texclude_hidden.help: Do not include refs that would be hidden by git-fetch, git-receive-pack or git-upload-pack by consulting the appropriate fetch.hideRefs, receive.hideRefs or uploadpack.hideRefs configuration along with transfer.hideRefs (see git-config(1))

log\tgrep.help: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that matches the specified pattern (regular expression)

log\tgrep_reflog.help: Limit the commits output to ones with reflog entries that match the specified pattern (regular expression)

log\tinvert_grep.help: Limit the commits output to ones with a log message that do not match the pattern specified with --grep=<pattern>

log\toneline.help: This is a shorthand for "--pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit" used together
